completion_data.completion_summary: Registered validate-meta-write.sh in the PostToolUse hook matcher, widened its path coverage to .claude/scripts/** and .claude/hooks/** and rewrote its advisory message to name the source store as the correct edit target (removing the backwards /implement exemption), and created one canonical source-store-deploy-boundary.md rule file referenced by a one-line MUST NOT bullet in all 15 implementer-agent contracts, collapsing two pre-existing duplicate prose copies of the rule (meta-builder-agent.md and commands/meta.md) into pointers.

memory_candidates.content: In-repo pattern for durably encoding a cross-cutting rule across many agent contracts without duplicating prose: author ONE core rule file under agent-system/extensions/core/rules/ (register in manifest.json's provides.rules AND merge-sources/claudemd.md's Rules References list), then append a single one-line MUST NOT bullet in each affected agent contract pointing at it (e.g. 'see .claude/rules/<file>.md; do X instead'). When collapsing a pre-existing duplicate prose statement of the same rule, preserve any genuinely agent-specific clause inline rather than deleting it outright -- only the general explanation moves to the pointer.

A PostToolUse hook (e.g. validate-meta-write.sh) only receives a file_path argument and can never know task type, lifecycle stage, or repository identity. It is structurally an advisory nudge on path SHAPE only, never a backstop for target-root correctness. When writing or reviewing such hooks, never let their advisory message overclaim enforcement -- state the limitation explicitly in both the hook's own comments and any rule file that references it.

This repo's .claude/ tree is regenerated from agent-system/extensions/** by a Lua file-copy engine (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/loader.lua), not through the Claude Code Write/Edit tool call path. Any PostToolUse hook gated on Write|Edit therefore structurally cannot fire during a deploy/reload, so widening such a hook's path coverage carries no risk of interfering with deploy -- no carve-out is ever needed for the loader itself.
